title: Ops Resilience: The Lights Go Out
description: The intrusion was real. Parts of Singapore have lost power. The attacker has taken control of 12 substations. You have minutes to isolate them and secure the rest of the grid.
storyContext: Lights went out across Jurong and Tuas at 3:14am. Tampines and Bedok followed within minutes. The attacker now controls 12 substations. Red phones ringing. The Minister wants a situation report in 30 minutes. Every second they stay connected, they can reach more of the grid.

software-engineer.title: Stop the Spread
software-engineer.instruction: The attacker controls 12 substations and is moving to the next ones. You can see their target. How do you stop the spread?
software-engineer.hint: When a threat is actively spreading, stopping it fast matters more than understanding it perfectly. Speed of containment beats elegance.

options.label: Cut all connections to the 12 compromised stations immediately. They switch to manual control. Stops the spread but those stations can't be managed remotely until cleaned.
Set up decoy systems on the attacker's likely next targets. Let them think they've succeeded while you watch. Risky if they don't take the bait.
Emergency reset of every password across the entire grid. Locks them out if they're using stolen logins — but changing passwords on live critical systems mid-crisis is risky.
Flood the network with fake signals to confuse the attacker's tools. Buys time, but makes it harder for your own team to see what's real.

data-scientist.title: Reconstruct How They Got In
data-scientist.instruction: Leadership needs to know how the attacker entered and what they've touched. Reconstruct the intrusion timeline. Arrange the steps.
data-scientist.hint: Gather all the evidence first, then arrange it chronologically. Work backward from the attack moment to find where it started.

items.label: Gather logs from every network device, login system, and station controller
Arrange all events chronologically using timestamps
Find the very first infected device — the earliest unusual event
Trace how the attacker moved from device to device
Extract the attacker's digital fingerprints to block them from returning

cloud-engineer.title: Isolate the Network Zones
cloud-engineer.instruction: Split the grid's network into isolated sections to stop the attacker jumping between them. Zone 1: fully cut off. Zones 2-3: partially restricted. Zone 4: continues normally.
cloud-engineer.hint: The most dangerous zones get the most restrictions. The further from the threat, the more normal operations can continue.

items.label: The 12 Compromised Stations — attacker is in control
Neighbouring Stations — at risk of being targeted next
Central Control Room — where commanders manage the grid
Office IT Network — admin and support systems
Contractor Remote Access — external vendors with maintenance access
